claims.text: Eutectic high-entropy alloys can have dual-phase fcc/B2 lamellar colonies.
The baseline eutectic alloy has high strength but low room-temperature tensile ductility.
Low room-temperature tensile ductility in the baseline alloy is caused by microcracking along internal lamellar boundaries.
A high-temperature treatment near 900°C followed by aging near 650°C can form δ lamellae and fine γ″ precipitates.
The proposed two-step treatment can be applied directly to an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The treatment should be performed under an inert atmosphere.
AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic alloy chemistries can support the proposed coherent δ/γ″ precipitation sequence.
The two-step treatment will produce finely dispersed coherent δ lamellae and γ″ particles within the lamellar colonies.
The new precipitates will modify or reinforce the interphase boundaries of the eutectic lamellar colonies.
Coherent precipitate/matrix interfaces enhance dislocation transmission while also providing effective dislocation pinning.
The proposed precipitates relieve local stress concentrations at lamellar interfaces.
Relieving interfacial stress concentrations reduces microcrack initiation and promotes strain hardening.
The two-step treatment will improve both room-temperature tensile strength and ductility relative to the untreated lamellar-colony baseline.
The treatment may improve tensile elongation by more than 50% relative to the untreated baseline.
The treatment may increase yield strength by approximately 1 GPa.
The intervention is effective only in eutectic alloys whose chemistries support controlled coherent precipitation.
Processing deviations can cause precipitate coarsening or formation of brittle secondary phases.
Identically prepared treated and untreated specimens can be compared using TEM, EBSD, room-temperature tensile testing, and fractography.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in both yield strength and tensile ductility would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to form the predicted coherent precipitates would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is called a thermo-mechanical treatment, but the specified protocol contains only thermal annealing and aging and identifies no mechanical-deformation step.
